messages:
samantha.li: hi folks, newbie question — I accepted the org invite but private repos still say I don't have access. invite was sent to my personal github (samanthali) not my work account (s.li@redwood.ai). what should I do? :confused:

ryan.ops: welcome! we typically require SAML SSO + 2FA. if you have two GitHub accounts it's easiest to add your work email to the account you want to use and verify it, then accept SSO on that account.

samantha.li: i added s.li@redwood.ai as a secondary email to my personal account and verified it. i still don't see the org banner to Authorize SSO.

melissa.dev: hey samantha — sometimes the invite gets attached to the account that matched at invite time. If the invite landed to the other account, we can re-send to the address tied to your preferred account. Can you confirm which username you want to use for work?

samantha.li: prefer using my personal username (samanthali) but with work email attached. is there a risk of leaking personal repos into the org if i use that?

ryan.ops: good Q. Your personal repos remain private unless you transfer them. Org membership doesn't automatically move personal repos. If you want to keep separation, just ensure your ssh keys and PATs are on the work-mapped account only.

samantha.li: i see the invite on my other account (s-li-redwood). should i accept there and then delete that account later? seems messy.

melissa.dev: easiest path: pick one account to keep as your work account. If you want the personal username as your public identity, you can: 1) add work email to that account 2) verify + accept SSO 3) request we reassign the invite to that account (we can trigger reprovision). If you want to consolidate, transfer any personal repos you care about to a new personal org before giving the work account org access.

samantha.li: ok i'm going to add work email to samanthali and verify. quick Q: do i need a PAT or SSH for day-to-day?

devex-bot: onboarding tip: we support SSH keys (recommended) and HTTPS w/ PAT. For actions/CI you may also need `workflow` scope on PAT. Always create PAT after SSO authorization. Docs: https://intranet.redwood.ai/onboarding/github.

samantha.li: added and verified. still no banner. i did sign out/in.

ryan.ops: can you paste the account username you are signed into (just the username)? we'll check which account the invite is attached to.

samantha.li: signed in as `samanthali`. invite email was to `s-li-redwood`.

melissa.dev: thanks. i'll resend invite to `samanthali` email mapping now and enable SSO mapping. one sec.

melissa.dev: invite resent. you should see an email and the org banner now. Accept the invite and click 'Authorize SSO'.

samantha.li: got the invite and banner, clicked Authorize SSO. i can clone private repos now but pushing fails with 403 via HTTPS.

ryan.ops: 403 on push usually means your PAT/credentials don't have write access or you authenticated with the other account's token. If you use HTTPS, do: `git remote -v` and `git credential-osxkeychain erase` (or whatever OS helper) to remove old creds, then create a new PAT after SSO with `repo` scope. If using SSH, ensure your public key is registered (Settings -> SSH and GPG keys).

samantha.li: i was using an old PAT from the other account. revoked it and created a new PAT with `repo` and `workflow` scopes. push works now :tada:

security-bot: reminder: per policy, PATs must be rotated every 90 days and not checked into repos. Use secrets manager for CI.

melissa.dev: added you to team `eng` and subteam `eng/backend` — that gives write to the backend repos. if you need infra access, ping ops with the repo and we can add you to `eng-infra` groups.

samantha.li: thanks all — one more tiny thing: the CODEOWNERS file forbids direct pushes to main for some repos. do i need a PR template or approvals?

melissa.dev: yes a quick note: backend repos require 1 reviewer from codeowners and tests passing. see CONTRIBUTING.md in each repo.

samantha.li: got it, reading docs now. really appreciate the help :heart:

devex-bot: next steps checklist: 1) verify work email on GitHub 2) authorize org SSO 3) create PAT post-SSO or add SSH key 4) confirm team membership 5) read CONTRIBUTING.md. If any step fails, ping #devex.

melissa.dev: closing this thread soon — welcome to Redwood! :wave:
